images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of GSTAR. (a) Text-to-image generation samples spanning portraits, landscapes, typography, and structured layouts. (b) Image editing examples: given an original image and a text instruction, our model produces faithful edits while preserving unrelated content (original→\rightarrowedited). (c) Average benchmark score comparison, where our GSTAR-Pro-8B achieves competitive performance against leading proprietary, diffusion, and discrete autoregressive models. (d) Quality vs. latency at1024×10241024\times 1024resolution, where our GSTAR-Pro-8B and GSTAR-Flash-1.7B models achieve competitive quality with significantly lower latency.

Figure 2:Grouped tokenization and spatial–group co-scaling. (a) A semantic encoder maps an
image to a spatially compressed latent grid, and group-wise quantization represents each position
with G discrete codes. Lossless 2 × 2 packing converts the native 32× grid into an effective 64×
interface, reducing the number of global autoregressive steps by four while increasing the codes per
step from G to 4G. (b) Jointly scaling spatial compression and group size preserves the nominal
information capacity per image while shortening the global sequence.

Figure 3:Comparison of intra-group prediction heads. Given the backbone context ht, (a) causal
autoregressive decoding captures dependencies among codes but requires repeated, expensive head
evaluations, while (b) parallel prediction head is fast but ignores these dependencies, risking
inconsistent code combinations. (c) Our semi-autoregressive head addresses both limitations: a par-
allel feature generator performs the heavy computation once, and a lightweight single-layer causal
Transformer models dependencies during sequential sampling.
